approach: Two root causes, two fixes. (1) The email allow-list scan runs only in admit(), after the producer has finished and the candidate commit is built, so the producer gets no feedback and the refusal names no line. Fix: add a line-numbered variant of the scan in athena-gate content.rs (reusing disallowed_emails and the configured PersonalData), wrap it in admission.rs, and call it from producer_loop (via a helper in run/candidate.rs) right after a successful producer invocation on the snapshot's working diff (base commit vs work_tree_tree). A finding stops the job with closing.happened = failure("admission refused the change: <path>:<line> adds an email address outside the allow-list"). Admission keeps its own scan as the backstop. (2) Introspection's earlier-case search narrows only by class_of_work and category, and it never sees an outcome's refusal reason. A refused job whose class_of_work or category differs from the new event's is not passed to the model, so the model picks 'new', and apply_answer then drops every earlier case, because a case counts only if it was passed in and sits in the chosen existing class. Fix: read_records also keeps each job's outcome reason (Records.job_reasons, job id to reason); admission.rs exposes the refusal-reason key (the rule text with the leading path or path:line token removed); narrow_cases puts cases whose job's outcome records the same refusal reason as the event first, then the class/category matches, still capped at CASE_CAP. apply_answer is not changed. Once the matching cases are passed in, the model can pick their existing class and they pass its checks. Add one producer.md line, update docs/system-facts.md's producer budget line, and add a CHANGELOG entry naming both root causes.

decisions.choice: Run the scan in producer_loop right after a successful invocation, as a hard stop (Flow::Stop with a failure reason), not a send-back.
decisions.reason: The request says a disallowed address 'fails the producer's own run and names the file and line'. Reusing the admission rule means no new rule: it only moves earlier. The reason carries the 'admission refused the change: ' prefix, so introspection's matcher sees the same text as an admission refusal.

rejected.option: Send the finding back to the producer like an unmet criterion.
rejected.why: The request asks for a failed run; a send-back would let the run pass and changes the send-back contract and PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS accounting.

rejected.option: Add it as a configured check in athena.toml.
rejected.why: Config and workflows are out of scope. A configured check also runs after candidate build, not in the producer loop.

decisions.choice: Add a line-numbered scan in athena-gate content.rs that parses `git diff -U0` hunk headers (`@@ -a,b +c,d @@`) and calls the existing disallowed_emails.
decisions.reason: Git::added_lines returns no line numbers, and the failure must name the line. Parsing hunk headers counts only added lines, so a pre-existing address in a modified file is not blamed on the producer. It uses the same allow-list function, so there is one email rule.

rejected.option: Scan whole changed files from the snapshot and report the line numbers found.
rejected.why: It would flag addresses that were already in the base.

rejected.option: Change Git::added_lines in athena-git to return line numbers.
rejected.why: It widens the change to a shared API with other callers; content.rs can parse the diff itself through the public run_bytes.

decisions.choice: Match earlier cases on the job outcome's refusal reason through a new Records.job_reasons map (job to reason). Leave CaseRow and apply_answer unchanged.
decisions.reason: CaseRow is built as a struct literal in tests, and it has no refusal reason. The reason lives in the job's outcome record, which read_records already visits to build Records.jobs, so the map is the smallest addition. Fixing what narrow_cases passes in is the origin of the fault. apply_answer's drop rule is right (a case outside the chosen class, or never shown, should not be cited), and the cases now pass it.

rejected.option: Keep earlier cases in apply_answer when the model picks 'new'.
rejected.why: A 'new' class has no earlier cases by definition, so this would record contradictory data; the model chose 'new' only because it was shown nothing.

rejected.option: Add a refusal_reason field to CaseRow, or to the introspection record.
rejected.why: It changes a record or row shape that is round-tripped and constructed in tests for no gain; the outcome already holds the reason.

decisions.choice: The match key is the refusal text with the leading path or path:line token removed, taken from the segments after 'admission refused the change: ' split on '; '. admission.rs owns the prefix and rule-text constants, and admit() and the in-loop scan both use them.
decisions.reason: The two stored refusals name different files, so an exact match on the full detail would never match. One owner for the strings stops the matcher drifting from the rule text.

rejected.option: Substring-match the fixed email phrase only.
rejected.why: It would not cover other admission rules, which the request asks for ('the admission refusal reason').

decisions.choice: No change to athena-cap-change checks()/admit(); a unit test there pins that the producer prompt carries the new line.
decisions.reason: The scan is a core pipeline rule using the repository's [personal_data] config, so it is not a capability check.

risks.risk: The new tests and the plan's own diff contain email-like text. The scan would then fail the producer's own run, or admission would, on the change that adds the scan.
risks.mitigation: Build addresses in tests from fragments with concat(). Use only allow-listed forms (the noreply@ local part, @example.com) in docs, the CHANGELOG and the prompt. The prompt line says 'emails' with no address.

risks.risk: The producer.md line pushes the producer prompt set over its 1300-token budget (it has 43 tokens left, ceil(bytes/3)).
risks.mitigation: Keep the line to about 100 bytes (about 34 tokens), run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`, and update the docs/system-facts.md line to the computed value.

risks.risk: Hunk-header parsing mis-numbers lines (for example a hunk with zero added lines, or a binary file, or a path with unusual characters).
risks.mitigation: Parse only `@@ ... +c[,d] @@` for the new start and count. Take only lines starting '+' (not '+++'). Skip `+++ /dev/null`. Unit-test an added file, a modified file with two hunks, and a deletion. An unparsable hunk gives no finding, because admission still catches the address.

risks.risk: The refusal-reason key matches cases that should not match, or crowds out class/category cases in the cap of 5.
risks.mitigation: The key is the exact rule text after the path token, and matching cases are listed first, so at most CASE_CAP are shown. Test that an event with a different refusal does not pull in the cases, and that the existing class/category narrowing test still passes.

risks.risk: A retry of a job that failed in-loop has less to seed from than one refused at admission.
risks.mitigation: See the open question. The failure reason is in admission-refusal form and carries file:line, so the retry brief sees it.

risks.risk: read_records now parses `reason` from outcome files; an old or odd outcome file could fail to parse.
risks.mitigation: The field is #[serde(default)], and OutcomeRow does not deny unknown fields, so older files still parse.

demonstrations.method: A test in run/tests.rs wraps base_script() so the Producer turn edits README.md to three lines, with an address outside the allow-list on line 3. The address is built from fragments with concat(), so the test file does not trip the scan it tests. It calls athena.ask(...) then athena.go(job, AcceptedBy::User, &Lines) and asserts the job finishes Failed. It also asserts the reason contains 'README.md:3' and 'adds an email address outside the allow-list', that no UI line starts with 'candidate' (the failure came before candidate_stage), and that no verifier ran.
demonstrations.observes: Finished.state is Failed and the reason names README.md:3; no 'candidate  ' line was emitted.
demonstrations.fails_without: On base code, no scan runs in the producer loop. The job reaches candidate_stage and prints a 'candidate  README.md (modified)' line. Admission then refuses with 'README.md adds an email address outside the allow-list', which has no ':3', so the line-number assertion and the no-candidate-line assertion both fail.

demonstrations.method: A unit test in introspect.rs's tests module writes, in a tempdir, the stored records (via AnyRecord::to_json and canonical_path): two failed outcomes (reason 'admission refused the change: <path> adds an email address outside the allow-list', different files), two recorded introspections of those jobs in one registered class, and the failure-class record. The cases' class_of_work differs from the new event's, which is the base-code gap. It calls read_records(dir), builds the Event with what = '<title>: admission refused the change: <other path>:<line> adds an email address outside the allow-list', and calls narrow_cases. It asserts both case ids are returned. It then passes those ids to athena.apply_answer with an Answer that picks the existing class and cites both. It asserts record.earlier_cases has both ids, new_class is false, and dropped_ids is empty. A second narrow_cases assertion uses an event with a different refusal and asserts neither case is returned.
demonstrations.observes: The narrowed list holds both case ids; the record has two earlier_cases and new_class false.
demonstrations.fails_without: On base code narrow_cases filters only on class_of_work and category, so the list is empty. The ids are then not in passed_cases and apply_answer drops both into dropped_ids, so the narrowed-list and earlier_cases assertions fail. The test uses only APIs that exist on base (read_records, narrow_cases, apply_answer), so it compiles and fails on an assertion, not on a missing symbol.

open_questions: records/ is absent from my copy, so I could not read introspection 20261025-074235-4nff or the outcomes of 9e8t and akwq. The cause is read from the code, not from those records: either narrow_cases excluded the earlier cases (different class_of_work or category), or the model chose 'new' and apply_answer dropped them. The producer should confirm from the code and name it in the change; the fix covers the first cause, which is the one visible in the code.

The in-loop failure leaves closing.candidate empty, whereas an admission refusal keeps a candidate with violations. I have not read how retry (tree_seed, timeout_seed, resume_seed) seeds from a failed job. The producer should check that a retry of an in-loop failure still gets the working tree or the finding. If it does not, keep the work by calling keep_timed_out_work-style retention.

The brief's deliverables omit crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs, where producer_loop lives. The plan adds it, since the call has to be in the loop, and docs/system-facts.md, because the budget test needs it. Please confirm both are acceptable.
